component.name: Whatsie
component.summary: Feature-rich WhatsApp Web client for the Linux desktop

description.p: Whatsie is a native Linux desktop client for WhatsApp Web, built on Qt 6 and QtWebEngine. It brings WhatsApp out of the browser tab and into a proper desktop application — lightweight and fast, with system integration, privacy controls, and customization options a plain browser cannot offer.

ul.li: Light, dark and follow-system themes, kept in step with WhatsApp Web
Native desktop notifications with contact avatars
System-tray icon with an unread badge, mute and do-not-disturb
Voice, video and screen-share calls (Wayland via the desktop portal)
Built-in download manager with history; drag-and-drop and paste of attachments
Spell check for your system language
App lock with a passcode and configurable lock on start, on hide, or after idle
Privacy blur to hide message text and media until you hover
Per-site camera, microphone and location permissions
HTTP / SOCKS5 network proxy with authentication
Autostart at login and start minimized to the tray
Single instance with multiple-account profiles
Zoom and interface scaling, plus a keyboard-shortcuts sheet
One-click bug reporting with diagnostics, no messages included

screenshot.caption: WhatsApp Web in a native desktop window
Appearance — themes, zoom and interface scale
Privacy — per-site permissions and screen lock

description.p: Whatsie 6 is a from-scratch rewrite on Qt 6.11 and QtWebEngine — lighter, faster and more private. Highlights:

ul.li: Themes that follow WhatsApp Web, with a reliable light/dark toggle
Native notifications with avatars and a system-tray unread badge
Voice, video and screen-share calls, with a reliable full-screen exit
A real downloads manager; drag-and-drop and paste of attachments
A hardened passcode app lock, privacy blur and per-site permissions
Spell check, network proxy, autostart and multiple-account profiles
Zoom, interface scaling and a one-click bug reporter with diagnostics

description.p: Minor release focused on build-system and runtime stability improvements:

ul.li: Migrated primary build workflow to CMake + Ninja for Qt 6 development
Refined Qt 6 WebEngine integration and permission handling paths
Improved desktop notification delivery via org.freedesktop.Notifications on Qt 6
Improved session persistence via consistent profile handling
Updated in-app theme application logic for current WhatsApp Web changes

description.p: Major release — Qt 6 port with significant improvements:

ul.li: Ported to Qt 6 and QtWebEngine 6 for better performance and long-term support
Reliable light/dark theme toggle without requiring a page reload
Persistent named WebEngine profile with proper cookie and storage handling
Improved permission handling for camera, microphone, and notifications
Centralised profile management and refactored codebase
